questions.question: An LP has the form $\max\,\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\le\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$. What is its augmented form?
When an LP $\max\,3x_1+5x_2$ with two $\le$ constraints is written in augmented form with slacks $s_1,s_2$, what is the objective?
An LP with $\le$ constraints and $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ is rewritten in augmented form. How does this affect the set of allowed original decisions $\boldsymbol{x}$?
options: It is unchanged; only the algebraic representation differs.
It shrinks, since every constraint is now written as an equation.
It grows, since the slack variables add new choices.
It shrinks to plans that use every resource completely.

questions.question: For a feasible original vector $\boldsymbol{x}$ of an LP with constraints $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\le\boldsymbol{b}$, how many slack vectors $\boldsymbol{s}$ make $(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{s})$ feasible in augmented form?
options: None, since the equations would need $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ exactly.
Infinitely many, since $\boldsymbol{s}$ is only required to be $\ge0$.
As many as there are constraints, one for each of the rows.

questions.question: In the augmented form $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}+\boldsymbol{s}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$, $\boldsymbol{s}\ge0$, which part carries the original inequalities $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\le\boldsymbol{b}$?
options: The objective, which is unchanged in the original variables
The nonnegativity $\boldsymbol{s}\ge0$ of the slack variables

questions.question: An LP has 3 decision variables, 4 functional constraints of type $\le$ and nonnegativity of all variables. In augmented form, how many variables and functional equations are there?
options: 3 variables, since slacks are not counted, and 4 equations
4 variables, one per row, and 3 equations

questions.question: For the production LP $\max\,3x_s+2x_t$ subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$ (finishing hours), $x_s+x_t\le80$ (carpentry hours), $x_s\le40$ (soldier demand), $x_s,x_t\ge0$, which system is the augmented form with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$?

For the production LP $\max\,3x_s+2x_t$ subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$ (finishing hours), $x_s+x_t\le80$ (carpentry hours), $x_s\le40$ (soldier demand), $x_s,x_t\ge0$, what is the augmented vector $(x_s,x_t,s_1,s_2,s_3)$ for the plan $(x_s,x_t)=(20,60)$?

A vector $(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{s})$ satisfies all equations $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}+\boldsymbol{s}=\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$, but one slack is $s_2=-3$. What does this say about $\boldsymbol{x}$ in the original LP?
options: It violates constraint 2, using 3 units more than allowed.
It is feasible, since all of the equations are satisfied.
It satisfies constraint 2 and leaves 3 units unused.
It is feasible but not optimal, as one slack is negative.

questions.question: An LP contains the constraints $x_1+x_2\le6$ and $x_1-x_2=1$ with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. How should it be written as a system of equations with nonnegative slacks?

For an LP $\max\,\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\le\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$, the augmented form is solved and $(\boldsymbol{x}^*,\boldsymbol{s}^*)$ is optimal. What follows for the original LP?
options: $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ is feasible but may not be optimal.
$\boldsymbol{x}^*$ is optimal with the same objective value.
$\boldsymbol{x}^*$ is optimal, but its value is $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}^*$ plus the slacks.

questions.question: For the augmented constraints $2x_1+x_2+s_1=10$, $x_1+3x_2+s_2=15$, all variables nonnegative, a feasible vector has $s_1=s_2=0$. What are $x_1$ and $x_2$?
An LP has the constraints $x_1+x_2\le6$ and $x_1\le4$ with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. A modeller writes them as $x_1+x_2+s=6$ and $x_1+s=4$, using a single slack $s\ge0$ for both. What goes wrong?
options: Nothing, since slacks may be shared when they are nonnegative.
The model gains plans that violate one of the two original constraints.
The objective changes, since $s$ now appears twice.
The constraints force equal unused amounts, removing feasible plans.

questions.question: For the production LP $\max\,3x_s+2x_t$ subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$ (finishing hours), $x_s+x_t\le80$ (carpentry hours), $x_s\le40$ (soldier demand), $x_s,x_t\ge0$, which augmented vector $(x_s,x_t,s_1,s_2,s_3)$ is feasible and has the largest profit $3x_s+2x_t$ among these?

For the production LP $\max\,3x_s+2x_t$ subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$ (finishing hours), $x_s+x_t\le80$ (carpentry hours), $x_s\le40$ (soldier demand), $x_s,x_t\ge0$ (optimum 180 at $(20,60)$), a modeller forgets the slack $s_3$ and writes the demand constraint as $x_s=40$. What is the optimal profit of this flawed model?
